task_completion.description: Open the 'Leaf' sample image in Fiji/ImageJ.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The Fiji/ImageJ application window is visible showing an image of a green leaf (File > Open Samples > Leaf).

task_completion.description: Convert the image to a binary (black and white) format suitable for skeletonization.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The leaf image appears as a high-contrast black and white mask (often via Process > Binary > Make Binary or Thresholding).

task_completion.description: Apply the skeletonization process to the binary image.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The leaf veins are reduced to 1-pixel wide white lines on a black background (Process > Binary > Skeletonize).

task_completion.description: Perform the 'Analyze Skeleton' command to extract branch and junction data.
task_completion.visual_evidence: The 'Analyze Skeleton' dialog box is used, and a 'Results' or 'Branch information' table appears containing columns like '# Branches' and '# Junctions'.

task_completion.description: Export the analysis results to the specified CSV file path.
task_completion.visual_evidence: A 'Save As' dialog or file explorer shows the results being saved to '~/ImageJ_Data/results/skeleton_analysis.csv' with the required columns.

integrity.visual_evidence: Screenshots show the mouse cursor interacting with Fiji menus (File, Process, Analyze) and dialog windows.

integrity.description: The results in the CSV are derived from the image analysis, not manually typed.
integrity.visual_evidence: The values in the final CSV or results table match the complexity of the skeletonized image (should have >20 branches and >5 junctions).

integrity.description: The agent used the specific 'Leaf' sample image as required.

privileged_info_for_vlm: The 'Leaf' sample is a standard Fiji image.
